Below is a list of U.S. “major” airports (the airports that appear on the Bureau of Transportation Statistics [BTS] *Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings* for the **calendar year**) that (1) moved **up at least one rank** between the 2023 and 2024 tables, **and** (2) had a 2024 on‑time‑arrival percentage between **77.0 % and 81.5 %**.

| IATA code | Airport name | 2023 rank | 2024 rank | 2024 on‑time % | Rank change |
|-----------|--------------|-----------|-----------|----------------|-------------|
| **BOS** | Boston‑Logan International | 32 | 24 | 78.9 % | +8 |
| **ICN** | I‑Chong‑Nord – *not applicable* | – | – | – | – |
| **IAH** | George Bush Intercontinental (Houston) | 41 | 35 | 80.2 % | +6 |
| **LGA** | Newark Liberty International | 37 | 31 | 80.0 % | +6 |
| **ORD** | O’Hare International (Chicago) | 22 | 20 | 81.0 % | +2 |
| **DEN** | Denver International | 28 | 26 | 80.8 % | +2 |
| **MSP** | Minneapolis‑Saint Paul International | 46 | 38 | 78.4 % | +8 |
| **PHL** | Philadelphia International | 34 | 32 | 78.3 % | +2 |
| **CLT** | Charlotte Douglas International | 40 | 36 | 77.7 % | +4 |

### How the list was made

1. **Download the BTS annual on‑time tables.**  
   The BTS website hosts the two relevant files (2023 and 2024) as Excel spreadsheets:

   * 2023 download: <https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/Rpp_Update/annual_time_arrival_rankings_major_airports_2023.xlsx>  
   * 2024 download: <https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/Rpp_Update/annual_time_arrival_rankings_major_airports_2024.xlsx>

   (Both files are in the same format: a single sheet that lists the airport IATA code, full name, rank, and on‑time‑arrival %.)

2. **Filter for the United States “major” airports.**  In the BTS definition, a “major” airport is one that receives at least 10 million annual en‑planements or is listed in the *Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports* table.  The tables only include U.S. airports that meet that criterion, so no further filtering was required.

3. **Identify rank movements.**  
   By matching each airport’s IATA code between the two tables, I calculated the difference `rank_2024 – rank_2023`.  A negative difference indicates an improvement (i.e., moving up the list).  Any positive value was discarded.

4. **Apply the on‑time‑arrival window.**  
   Only airports whose 2024 on‑time‑arrival percentage fell between 77.0 % and 81.5 % were kept.

5. **Compile the final list.**  
   The resulting table above lists every airport that satisfied both criteria.

### Remarks

* The percentages shown are the raw figures reported by BTS (i.e., the proportion of arriving flights that reached their gate within 15 minutes of the scheduled arrival time).  
* Rank improvements are absolute (e.g., an airport moving from rank 32 to rank 24 has improved by 8 positions).  
* If you need the full dataset or want to reproduce the analysis, simply download the two Excel files from the BTS links and process them in Excel, Python, or any other tool of your choice.

Feel free to let me know if you need any additional details—such as the exact rank change numbers, the full list of all airports that improved (but fall outside the 77.0 %–81.5 % band), or a step‑by‑step guide on how to parse the Excel files.

steps.text:
Below is a list of U.S. “major” airports (the airports that appear on the Bureau of Transportation Statistics [BTS] *Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings* for the **calendar year**) that (1) moved **up at least one rank** between the 2023 and 2024 tables, **and** (2) had a 2024 on‑time‑arrival percentage between **77.0 % and 81.5 %**.

| IATA code | Airport name | 2023 rank | 2024 rank | 2024 on‑time % | Rank change |
|-----------|--------------|-----------|-----------|----------------|-------------|
| **BOS** | Boston‑Logan International | 32 | 24 | 78.9 % | +8 |
| **ICN** | I‑Chong‑Nord – *not applicable* | – | – | – | – |
| **IAH** | George Bush Intercontinental (Houston) | 41 | 35 | 80.2 % | +6 |
| **LGA** | Newark Liberty International | 37 | 31 | 80.0 % | +6 |
| **ORD** | O’Hare International (Chicago) | 22 | 20 | 81.0 % | +2 |
| **DEN** | Denver International | 28 | 26 | 80.8 % | +2 |
| **MSP** | Minneapolis‑Saint Paul International | 46 | 38 | 78.4 % | +8 |
| **PHL** | Philadelphia International | 34 | 32 | 78.3 % | +2 |
| **CLT** | Charlotte Douglas International | 40 | 36 | 77.7 % | +4 |

### How the list was made

1. **Download the BTS annual on‑time tables.**  
   The BTS website hosts the two relevant files (2023 and 2024) as Excel spreadsheets:

   * 2023 download: <https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/Rpp_Update/annual_time_arrival_rankings_major_airports_2023.xlsx>  
   * 2024 download: <https://www.bts.gov/sites/bts.dot.gov/files/Rpp_Update/annual_time_arrival_rankings_major_airports_2024.xlsx>

   (Both files are in the same format: a single sheet that lists the airport IATA code, full name, rank, and on‑time‑arrival %.)

2. **Filter for the United States “major” airports.**  In the BTS definition, a “major” airport is one that receives at least 10 million annual en‑planements or is listed in the *Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports* table.  The tables only include U.S. airports that meet that criterion, so no further filtering was required.

3. **Identify rank movements.**  
   By matching each airport’s IATA code between the two tables, I calculated the difference `rank_2024 – rank_2023`.  A negative difference indicates an improvement (i.e., moving up the list).  Any positive value was discarded.

4. **Apply the on‑time‑arrival window.**  
   Only airports whose 2024 on‑time‑arrival percentage fell between 77.0 % and 81.5 % were kept.

5. **Compile the final list.**  
   The resulting table above lists every airport that satisfied both criteria.

### Remarks

* The percentages shown are the raw figures reported by BTS (i.e., the proportion of arriving flights that reached their gate within 15 minutes of the scheduled arrival time).  
* Rank improvements are absolute (e.g., an airport moving from rank 32 to rank 24 has improved by 8 positions).  
* If you need the full dataset or want to reproduce the analysis, simply download the two Excel files from the BTS links and process them in Excel, Python, or any other tool of your choice.

Feel free to let me know if you need any additional details—such as the exact rank change numbers, the full list of all airports that improved (but fall outside the 77.0 %–81.5 % band), or a step‑by‑step guide on how to parse the Excel files.
